newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has refuted claims by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina that the party had initiated, while in power, giving transit facility to India and importing power from there.

Bangladesh's Water Resources Minister Abdur Razzak is expected to visit New Delhi sometimes at the end of the current month to talk with his Indian counterpart deatils of a water sharing accord between the two countries.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has called for correct and objective dissemination of news and views in the press to help her government's bid to solve national problems.

Commerce and Industries Minister Tofael Ahmed said the government would move ahead with reform and liberalisation programmes to allow the private sector a pivotal role in the economy. "The government will withdraw gradually from the business and remain as a facilitator," he said.

A large number of Burmese citizens have been intruding into Bangladeh territory and resorting to criminal activities in bordering areas, according to local leaders and traders in the Bandarban district in Chittagong Hill Tracts.

Country's export earnings during July-August stood at $766.73 million, exceeding the period's target by $36.73 million, officials said. Readymade garments alone fetched $405.59 million during the period.
A total of 23,834 overstaying Bangladeshis returned home from the United Arab Emirates till Wednesday.
